chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Writing rhythm and blues for publishers
summary: With Sid Wyche, Charlie Singleton and others, McRae composed and arranged songs that publishers placed with artists.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I started writing (inaudible) -- I think I picked up Charlie Singleton and a couple of other writers. Sid Wyche was a rock and roll writer. And we started doing rock and roll things, Pop. (inaudible)
Now you're speaking of the early 40's, but you mean rhythm and blues?
Rhythm and blues. Yeah, we started doing rhythm and blues.
Seems that it wasn't called rock and roll --
Who were some of the people you wrote for?
Oh, we did some things for -- We did -- I did some things with Jack Decree and all those different people like that. What we used to do -- write for the
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
publishers. We wasn't writing for the artists. The publishers used to call us and ask us if we had songs for this particular artist.
No. We were composing and doing the arrangements. Sometime I'd write the arrangements. Most of the time we would compose a song and write -- lay out the arrangements of a rock and roll thing.
Wasn't too much writing to do (inaudible) because they always used all the top musicians (inaudible).

And you didn't have to do too much writing, because most of the stuff was just the (inaudible), you know. Maybe a eight bar band, you know. An arrangement didn't call for too much writing, For that rock and roll stuff (inaudible).
Because most of it was repeat.
